currentContext.business: The Company markets and distributes networking and IT hardware in India, spanning home and business wireless solutions, network switches, surveillance equipment, network racks and structured cabling. It caters to the Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) and Small and Medium Business (SMB) segments in close alignment with System Integrators, while also targeting Government, Education, BFSI and Manufacturing verticals. Products are primarily procured from local EMS (Electronic Manufacturing Services) and ODM (Original Design Manufacturer) partners, with D-Link India granted exclusive rights/licence by the parent company to use the D-Link trademark on such locally manufactured products.

Consumer Networking Solutions: EAGLE PRO AI series AI-powered mesh networking systems
AQUILA PRO AI series AI-powered mesh networking systems
Unmanaged switches (Gigabit and Fast Ethernet variants)
Security components - CCTV cables and power supplies (SMPs)
ADDON Series accessories - mobile adapters, power strips, C-to-C cables
Enterprise Networking Solutions: Smart managed, fully managed, data center and industrial switches (10 to 100 Gigabit, PoE)
Enterprise wireless - access points, controllers and management software
Structured cabling - copper UTP/STP (Cat5, Cat6, Cat6A), fiber vertical and horizontal solutions, connectivity accessories
Datacenter solutions - high-density MPO and OM4/OM5 fiber
Network enclosures - wall-mount, floor-standing (indoor and outdoor IP66-rated) and smart racks

risks.note: The inability to stay up to date with changing technologies and the latest trends is detrimental to the business. Digitization is emerging as a disruptive force for customers, buyers and technology; combined with changes in delivery models and consumer spending patterns it could threaten growth in traditional IT spending and cause technology obsolescence. The Company must continuously review and upgrade its technology, resources and processes, and relies on strong R&D support from its parent company to stay ahead of the curve.

In a hyper-connected world, cybersecurity incidents that cause economic losses and/or breach company and personal information are a reality for any business. The Company relies on a robust intrusion prevention system and a strong risk management framework, and continuously evaluates the threat landscape.

The IT industry is highly competitive, with competition from local IT companies and MNC IT hardware companies having a sizable presence in low-cost technologies. This can lead to pressure on pricing and vendor consolidation, impacting Company growth and profitability, and new competitors are emerging from adjacent markets and distant geographies.

The functional currency is the Indian Rupee and volatility in exchange movements results in transaction and translation exposure. D-Link has substantial exposure to foreign-exchange risk on account of imports of finished traded products from its parent group companies, and cabling products are subject to fluctuations in raw material prices such as copper. Management predicts the USD position will continue to remain volatile; the Company follows a well-established hedging policy and does not undertake speculative hedging.

Supply chain volatility is a complex and ever-changing challenge. Global semiconductor supply chains were severely affected after the pandemic and faced further disruptions due to the Russia-Ukraine conflict; any sudden disruption of global and domestic supply chains poses a risk for the Company.

themes.title: Telecom & digital-infrastructure capex
themes.need: 5G monetization, FTTH and tower/fibre densification drive the connectivity cycle - and Q1FY27 repriced the optical leg outright. STLTECH booked order intake of INR 13,100cr in ONE quarter, 1.7x its entire FY26 order book, anchored by a multi-year $1.1bn hyperscaler deal running through FY29, taking the open order book to INR 18,618cr (up 2.4x QoQ) on revenue of INR 1,910cr (+87%) and EBITDA INR 397cr (+184%). It then raised guidance twice on the same call - EBITDA margin target from 20%-by-end-FY27 (already hit at 20.8% in Q1) to 23%, and Data-Center + Enterprise mix from 30% to 50% of FY27 revenue, after DC went from 1% of revenue in FY26 to 21%. The catch is supply, not demand: ex the anchor deal quarterly intake fell to ~INR 3,000cr from INR 7,000-8,000cr because 'we have to pick and choose the orders basis the capacity availability', with germanium and helium named as binding raw-material constraints. BHARTIARTL on ARPU + 5G; INDUSTOWER on tower rollout; SUYOG-tier on passive infra; GTPL/HFCL-tier on broadband + fibre; tariff hikes and rural FTTH are the near-term levers.
themes.driver: STLTECH's $1.1bn hyperscaler ramp against germanium/helium supply constraints and the raised 23% margin / 50% DC-mix guides; tariff-hike flow-through; 5G/FTTH capex; tower tenancy adds.

It caters to the Small Office/Home Office (SOHO) and Small and Medium Business (SMB) segments in close alignment with System Integrators, while also targeting Government, Education, BFSI and Manufacturing verticals. Products are primarily procured from local EMS (Electronic Manufacturing Services) and ODM (Original Design Manufacturer) partners, with D-Link India granted exclusive rights/licence by the parent company to use the D-Link trademark on such locally manufactured products.

products.title: Products & brands
products.body:
- **Consumer Networking Solutions:** EAGLE PRO AI series AI-powered mesh networking systems, AQUILA PRO AI series AI-powered mesh networking systems, Whole-home mesh systems, Wi-Fi 6 routers, AC routers, 4G LTE routers, Wireless N routers, Unmanaged switches (Gigabit and Fast Ethernet variants), Security components - CCTV cables and power supplies (SMPs), ADDON Series accessories - mobile adapters, power strips, C-to-C cables
- **Enterprise Networking Solutions:** Smart managed, fully managed, data center and industrial switches (10 to 100 Gigabit, PoE), Enterprise wireless - access points, controllers and management software, Nuclias network management platform, Structured cabling - copper UTP/STP (Cat5, Cat6, Cat6A), fiber vertical and horizontal solutions, connectivity accessories, Datacenter solutions - high-density MPO and OM4/OM5 fiber, Network enclosures - wall-mount, floor-standing (indoor and outdoor IP66-rated) and smart racks

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Indian IT hardware and networking industry is expected to witness robust growth in FY 2026-27, with government infrastructure projects and expansion of digital services ensuring a positive trajectory for networking products and hardware even if general IT spending sees more measured growth
- India IT spending grew by around 10% to 12% in 2025-26, supported by strong demand across key industries and continued expansion in cloud, AI and cybersecurity
- India IT hardware market estimated to grow at a CAGR of 7.1%, and the network equipment market expected to expand at a CAGR of 5.5% from 2024 to 2030 (Research & Markets)
- Gartner (April 2026) projects global IT spending to reach $6.31 trillion in 2026, up 13.5% year-on-year, driven by AI infrastructure, cloud ecosystems and digital modernisation
- Structured cabling demand outlook is promising, driven by escalating demand for higher bandwidths, accelerated digitization of the economy and significant government investment in infrastructure
- Government policy support - Digital India, Make in India and Production Linked Incentive (PLI) schemes - encouraging domestic manufacturing and increased local sourcing of components and finished products
- Demand pull from 5G rollout, data centres, cloud ecosystems, IoT expansion, hybrid work models and enterprise digitalisation; heightened focus on data localisation and cybersecurity creating additional opportunities
- Cost headwind: near-full utilisation of manufacturing capacities in Taiwan has caused extended lead times and sustained pricing pressure across global supply chains
- Cost headwind: rapid AI adoption has increased demand for semiconductors, high-performance computing components and memory, leading to notable escalation in memory pricing that influences overall hardware cost structures
- Cost headwind: USD volatility plus rising prices of essential raw materials such as plastics have increased production costs for cables and networking equipment, while higher global fuel costs have raised logistics, transportation and distribution expenses
- Competitive pressure from well-known international brands with larger economies of scale, price-led buying behaviour in India, and the presence of counterfeit products
- Company positioning: D-Link India is well positioned to benefit from these trends through its diversified product portfolio, strong distribution network and focus on locally manufactured offerings

capital_allocation.title: Strategy & capital allocation
capital_allocation.body:
- Growth strategy focused on expanding enterprise solutions, accelerating consumer adoption, strengthening industry collaborations, building strategic partnerships and operating with greater agility
- Deepening the 'Make in India' commitment by strengthening local manufacturing and sourcing, thereby contributing to employment generation, improving supply-chain flexibility and enabling a more agile response to changing market requirements
- Strategic shift towards outsourced/contract manufacturing within India through local EMS and ODM partners, using the Company's own brand names, proprietary designs, quality control and supervision - which management says is helping the Company grow faster
- Customer centricity - strengthening customer relationships and service excellence, with a countrywide distribution and support infrastructure and digital support channels
- Investing in talent development, leadership capabilities, digital transformation and customer service excellence to build a skilled and empowered workforce
- Embedding artificial intelligence into core product offerings (EAGLE PRO AI and AQUILA PRO AI mesh systems) as part of redefining connected living
- Environmental sustainability through an Electronic Waste Management Program, with e-waste collection centres for responsible disposal of end-of-life products, defective components and other electronic waste
- Strengthening efficiencies and supply chain resilience, and adopting adaptable strategies to navigate external challenges
- The Board retained the entire amount of profits for FY 2026 in the profit and loss account and did not propose any transfer to the general reserve, so surplus is returned to shareholders through dividends rather than reserve appropriation. Shareholder distribution is governed by a formally adopted Dividend Distribution Policy published on the Company's website; during the year the Board declared and paid an interim dividend and has recommended a final dividend together with a special dividend for shareholders' approval at the Annual General Meeting. Governance of capital deployment sits with an Audit Committee whose remit includes scrutiny of inter-corporate loans and investments, valuation of undertakings or assets, evaluation of internal financial controls and risk management systems, monitoring the end use of funds raised through public offers, and reviewing utilisation of loans, advances or investments by the holding company in the subsidiary above the prescribed threshold. Unclaimed dividends and the related shares are transferred to the Investor Education and Protection Fund as required.
